title: Recipes: Run, Check and Export a Site Setup

chapters.title: Recipes
chapters.subtitle: Run, check and export a site setup

steps.text: This video shows recipes in the admin: the catalog of ready-made recipes and how to run one, the editor that checks a recipe you paste in, and how to export your own setup as a recipe with a deployment plan.
Setting up a site by hand is slow, and no two sites end up the same.
A recipe is a ready-made script that creates content types, settings, roles and sample content in one go.
Run one to start a site, try a feature with sample content, or move a setup from a test site to a live one.

chapters.title: The recipe catalog
chapters.subtitle: Find a recipe and run it

steps.text: Open Tools, Recipes. Every recipe has a name, tags and a description of what it creates. The CrestApps Recipes feature adds the descriptions, so you know what a recipe does before you run it.
Type in the search box to find a recipe by name or tag. Here, the recipes about SQL.
Click Run, and confirm. A recipe changes the site, so read the description first, and try it on a copy of the site when you are not sure. The page reports the result when the recipe is done.

chapters.title: The recipe editor
chapters.subtitle: Suggestions and checks as you type

steps.text: To run a recipe you have, open Tools, Deployments, JSON Import. The editor suggests the names of the steps as you type, so you do not have to remember them.
It also describes each setting, and underlines a mistake before anything runs. When the recipe looks right, click Import.
To turn the setup of one site into a recipe for another, open Configuration, Import and Export, Deployment Plans. Add a plan, and give it a name.
Click Add Step. Each step is a kind of setup you can export, such as content types, settings, roles, users or templates. Add the steps you want, here all the roles.
Add the users step too, to carry the people of the site, then check the plan. A step can have options of its own, and a plan can have as many steps as it needs.
Click Execute, and choose to export the plan to a file. The file is a recipe that you can import on another site, in the JSON Import editor you just saw.
Start every new site the same way.
Try a feature with sample content.
Move a setup from a test site to a live site.
Keep a copy of a configuration you can restore.

Run a recipe from the catalog, check one you wrote in the editor, and export your own setup with a deployment plan, so the next site is ready in minutes. The user manual and the technical guide are linked in the description. Thanks for watching.
